Electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-whiplash front head restraints work collectively to protect occupants. The rear backup camera assists with parking and low-speed maneuvering in tight spaces.

With 74,340 miles on the odometer, this Golf Alltrack has proven its durability while remaining well within typical wear expectations. The vehicle presents a compelling option for buyers valuing AWD capability, practicality, and proven Volkswagen engineering in a fuel-efficient package.

Wi-Fi hotspot compatibility and MySubaru app integration keep you connected on the go, while the touchscreen interface ensures easy access to all media and navigation functions.

Built for all-weather capability, this Outback features full-time 4WD, delivering consistent traction and stability across diverse driving conditions. Its naturally aspirated 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine provides a reliable balance of power and efficiency, making it ideal for daily use and outdoor adventures alike. The vehicle’s performance setup ensures confidence behind the wheel in any environment.

Distance pacing cruise control with traffic stop-go, your ultimate co-pilot.

  • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.

With head-up display, important driving information - like speed and RPM's - displays on your windshield in your line of sight. The 2019 Subaru Outback 2.5i Limited blends the comfort of a premium wagon with the capability of a genuine SUV, and it has earned a fiercely loyal following as a result. Standard Symmetrical ALL-WHEEL DRIVE, generous ground clearance, and a spacious, practical cabin make it equally at home on snowy mountain roads, dirt trails to the campsite, and the daily commute. This example is finished in rich Abyss Blue Pearl over Titanium Gray perforated leather-trimmed upholstery, a handsome, sophisticated combination. It was ordered with the Moonroof and Navigation Package. That package adds a power moonroof, an 8-inch STARLINK navigation system, LED Steering Responsive Headlights, High Beam Assist, Reverse Automatic Braking, and an auto-dimming mirror with HomeLink. The Limited's standard Harman Kardon premium audio, heated front and rear seats, and power rear gate round out a genuinely upscale package. With the odometer hovering around the 33,300-mile mark, this Outback has averaged remarkably low mileage for its age. It is a ONE-OWNER vehicle with 17 service records on its CARFAX report, a clear sign of attentive ownership. WHY SHOPPERS BUY THIS MODEL The Outback has long been one of Subaru's most popular vehicles, and it has carved out a unique place in the market. It rides lower than a traditional SUV, making it easier to load cargo and more composed on the road, yet it offers ground clearance that rivals many SUVs. For drivers who want capability without the bulk, it's the ideal compromise. Standard Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive is a big part of the appeal. It continuously powers all four wheels for superior traction in rain, snow, and slush, and X-Mode adds even more control on slippery or steep terrain. For drivers in regions with real winters, it provides peace of mind that front-wheel-drive competitors simply can't match. Shoppers also value the Outback's reputation for safety, practicality, and longevity. Subaru reports that the vast majority of Outbacks sold in the last decade are still on the road, and the Outback consistently ranks among the best vehicles for resale value. It's a smart, sensible choice that is also genuinely fun to own. AUTOMOTIVE PRESS AND INDUSTRY RECOGNITION The 2019 Outback earned widespread praise from reviewers for its spacious, comfortable cabin, smooth ride, and standard all-wheel drive. Critics also highlighted its enormous cargo area and its long list of standard safety technology, noting that upper trims like the Limited begin to feel like genuine luxury crossovers. Its strong resale value and reputation for dependability were consistently cited as key advantages. 2019 IIHS TOP SAFETY PICK+, awarded to Outbacks equipped with the LED Steering Responsive Headlights found on this example. ALG 2019 RESIDUAL VALUE AWARD. Car and Driver EDITORS' CHOICE. Kelley Blue Book 2019 BEST RESALE VALUE AWARD, Mid-Size SUV/Crossover (2-Row). WARRANTY The odometer currently reads 33,332 miles, and its CARFAX report shows 17 service records. Subaru's basic and powertrain warranties have concluded based on age, but supplemental factory coverage remains in effect. Remaining Transferable Factory Coverage: Federal Emissions Warranty (specified major components): through May 22, 2027, or 80,000 miles, whichever occurs first. Covers specified major emissions components, including the catalytic converter and the engine control module. STANDARD FEATURES The 2.5i Limited is where the Outback steps firmly into near-luxury territory. Leather-trimmed upholstery covers all seats, and both the front and rear outboard seats are heated, so every passenger stays comfortable on cold mornings. The 12-speaker Harman Kardon premium audio system fills the cabin with rich, powerful sound, and a power rear gate and keyless access with push-button start add everyday convenience. The Limited also includes Blind-Spot Detection with Rear Cross-Traffic Alert, dual-zone automatic climate control, and 18-inch alloy wheels. Like every 2019 Outback, it comes standard with Subaru's EyeSight Driver Assist Technology. Perforated leather-trimmed upholstery. A premium look and feel throughout the cabin. Heated front and rear outboard seats. Winter comfort for passengers in both rows. 12-speaker Harman Kardon premium audio system. Rich, powerful, room-filling sound. Power rear gate. Easy access to the cargo area at the touch of a button. Keyless access with push-button start. Unlock and start the Outback without taking the key out of your pocket. Blind-Spot Detection with Rear Cross-Traffic Alert. Warns of vehicles in your blind spots and while backing out. Dual-zone automatic climate control. Personalized comfort for the driver and front passenger. 18-inch alloy wheels. A polished, upscale appearance. INSTALLED OPTIONS This Outback was ordered with Subaru's most popular upgrade package for the Limited, adding comfort, technology, and safety features that make every drive better. Standalone Features Auto-dimming exterior mirror with approach light. Reduces glare from headlights behind you and illuminates the ground as you approach. Its horizontally opposed design sits low in the chassis, lowering the center of gravity for better balance and stability. It delivers smooth, dependable power for everyday driving and highway cruising. The engine is paired with Subaru's Lineartronic continuously variable automatic transmission, which keeps the engine in its most efficient range for smooth, seamless acceleration. Symmetrical All-Wheel Drive continuously powers all four wheels, and X-Mode with Hill Descent Control adds confidence on slippery or steep terrain. With 8.7 inches of ground clearance, the Outback handles rutted roads and snowy driveways with ease. 2.5-liter Boxer four-cylinder engine with 175 horsepower and 174 lb-ft of torque.
